title: Sidney Bechet playing for beer; spelling of Rishack
summary: Rene recounts Bechet getting a clarinet as a Christmas gift and playing in clubs for cans of beer; Zander asks how the venue name Rishack is spelled.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: You were talking about Sidney that day.

Bechet, yeah. Now Sidney Bechet, the first clarinet was a Christmas gift, see? And he picked up, now I can't tell you, I don't think Bechet ever took less than one on the clarinet, because he didn't know how to read, you know? But boy, he's going to play clarinet. And you know what Bechet used to do? Bechet used to, I know you heard talk about Peter Lauer when he had a show on Claymore Street, between Cori and St. Louis, you remember that? Peter Lauer had that. Well Bechet was a fella, he liked it a bit. And you could, Bechet would be down on the street or seminar street, and he'd walk way up to a place, you know what they call, Reshack, you know what they talk about, like musicians? Bob Lyon and on the full year, Saratoga and Gravy. Well Bechet all you tell him, he'd get a can of beer, and he would carry his clarinet. At that time he had a C clarinet, and he carried his pocket all the way. And he sat there, right in that booth, and boy he'd play a nice clarinet. Everybody liked it, he'd start. And he would play for that can of beer. Now when he'd get dry, then he'd put his clarinet right in his pocket. You had to buy another can of beer, you'd get you that can for ten cents, you know? That big tumble is he's getting for nickel?
Oh, by the way to interrupt, I've tried to look up that name to see, to write it down, that Rishack or whatever it is, how, do you know how that's spelled?
No, the uh, the clundent had the barn on the Saratoga and...
